title: Grateful Dead Live at Curtis Hixon Convention Hall on 1973-12-19
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of the legendary 12/19/73 show, highlighted by a soaring Here Comes Sunshine and a mind‑blowing Nobody’s Fault → The Other One sequence.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑remastered SBD of Dick’s Picks Vol. 1 delivers pristine clarity that lets every nuance of the late‑1973 quintet shine.  Fans rave about the ecstatic Here Comes Sunshine, the thunderous Weather Report Suite and the legendary Nobody’s Fault → The Other One jam, while the first set is seen as solid but uneven.  Overall the performance is a high point of ’73 with a superbly mixed recording that makes it a must‑listen.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.6/5; most comments praise both the show (especially the second‑set jams) and the recording’s clarity, with only minor criticisms of a few first‑set songs.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Remastered by Charlie Miller from the original SBD tape; described as crystal‑clear, balanced and levelled.  No major drop‑outs or muffling noted – only the usual edits present in the official Dick’s Picks release, which do not affect this file.

standout_songs: Truckin' > Nobody's Fault But Mine > The Other One
poor_songs: Playing in the Band (aimless/average according to one reviewer)
Dire Wolf (described as flat by a reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is solid but uneven, with a few slower moments; the second set erupts into high‑energy jams and seamless segues that define the show’s lasting appeal.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for perfect guitar tone, tight lead work on Truckin' and driving the jam energy.
band_member_comments.Phil: His bass solo (Decon Jam) is highlighted as a centerpiece; many note his “bomb” at the perfect spot in the second‑set jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals and rhythm guitar are solid; one reviewer notes Bob’s leering, slow‑motion chords during the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux receives specific praise for “just‑right chords” that add an ethereal feel to the segues.
